quotes.text: If you treat it like a technical problem, you'll miss what's actually happening. You'll spend money on tools and miss the structural failure underneath because drift is a governance failure.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes configuration drift as an organizational governance failure rather than a tooling problem.

quotes.text: AI agents must operate within policy guardrails, not autonomously, not with broad permissions, not trusted to make security decisions without oversight. They generate proposals, policies validate those proposals, humans review the validated output.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States a clear operating model for safely using AI-generated infrastructure code.

quotes.text: The governance principle is elemental. Automation increases risk unless it increases control proportionally. When you automate a process you amplify the impact of errors.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise, memorable principle linking automation to the need for proportional control.

quotes.text: Terraform owns multi-cloud. Bicep owns Azure native. These tools aren't actually competing for the same crown anymore because they occupy different strategic positions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the strategic split between Terraform and Bicep in one clear statement.

quotes.text: Cognitive friction is real. It matters more than technical superiority. Teams didn't stay with arm JSON because it was a better tool. They stayed because the cost of switching was high and the inertia of what they already knew felt comfortable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Distills the main adoption lesson from the move from ARM templates to Bicep.

takeaways: Configuration drift from manual portal changes is a governance failure, and only declarative infrastructure as code makes the actual state visible, reviewable and correctable.
Bicep compiles to ARM JSON but removes its syntax noise, which is why new Azure projects default to it while legacy ARM templates persist because of switching costs.
AI agents can generate infrastructure code quickly, but it must flow through policy as code, human review and CI/CD so that automation never outpaces control.
hook: Portal clicks feel fast, but they quietly create configuration drift that breaks governance at scale. This episode is for Azure architects and platform teams deciding between ARM, Bicep and Terraform, and it explains how infrastructure as code, policy as code and guardrails keep both humans and AI agents under control.
